holes.axis_divergence: primary reduction bid=1 (extent 8192): fused=128 standalone=8192 (64x under); secondary reduction bid=3 (extent 4096): fused=128 standalone=4096 (32x under)
holes.explanation: CLEANEST repro of the root-cause class. Two independent user-tiled reductions in two SEPARATE top-level hl.tile loops (grid=[[0],[2]]) are folded by register_unrolled_reductions into ONE ReductionFact with m_block_ids=[0,2] (grid axes from BOTH disjoint loops) and secondary_reduction_block_ids=[3]. TritonUserTiledReductionHeuristic.get_seed_config sizes R_BLOCK via _reduction_rblock(env, fact, m_block) where m_block = _m_block_product(spec, fact) = product over ALL m_block_ids = 16*16 = 256. Each loop's program only holds ONE loop's M_BLOCK rows (16, not 256), so the true per-program footprint is [16, R_BLOCK], yet R_BLOCK is divided by the cross-loop product 256 -> budget 245760/(256*4)=240 -> prev_pow2 128. Checker reads GREEN (no floor-to-1, axes are tunable and >1). A/B de-fuse: each loop standalone sizes its reduction to full extent (8192/4096) with M_BLOCK NOT widened. Root cause: _m_block_product (helion/_compiler/autotuner_heuristics/triton.py:872) blindly multiplies grid blocks from grid axes belonging to DIFFERENT fused loops; its own docstring 'rows each program processes' has no single meaning for a multi-loop fact. Same class as round-4 finding-2 (cross-loop residency leak) but on the REDUCTION R_BLOCK path, not the apply-loop denominator. Out-of-scope predicates ruled out: reduced axes are contiguous inner dims (not STRIDED-DIM0), backed (not JAGGED), RESIDENT not grid (not PARTIAL_GRID).

One fact, m_block_ids=[0,3]. _m_block_product = m_axis(0)=16 * m_axis(3)=1 = 16. The Q reduction's program holds [1, R_BLOCK] (its grid axis 3 is pinned 1), so it could hold the full 16384 persistent (64KB < 240KB). But R_BLOCK is divided by the COLLAPSE loop's CTA=16: extent_held fails (16*16384*4=1MB > ROW_PERSIST 240KB) so it streams at budget 245760/(16*4)=3840 -> prev_pow2 2048. The collapse loop's occupancy CTA (correct, 64 in _build_block_sizes) leaks into a DIFFERENT loop's reduction sizing. m-collapse override correctly did NOT fire (primary backed), but the cross-loop m_block_product still contaminates. Verified via instrumented probe k2_debug.py / k3 probe: fused m_block_product=16, standalone=1.

sweeps.narrative:
STRATEGY=NOVELTY (multi-loop fusion). I minted 10 fresh kernels (plus 14 standalone de-fuse partners) targeting un-sampled cross-products, ran the mechanical checker AND the A/B de-fuse divergence on every one, and instrumented _m_block_product / _reduction_rblock directly (k2_debug.py, k3 probe) to nail the arithmetic.

FOUND a systematic NEW hole class (4 confirmed instances: K3, K4, K7, K9; K10 is the cleanest minimal repro): when MULTIPLE reduction loops fuse into ONE user-tiled ReductionFact (register_unrolled_reductions folds all tiled reduction axes across all graphs into a single fact with secondaries), the fact's m_block_ids contains grid axes from DISJOINT loops, and _m_block_product (triton.py:872) cross-multiplies them. _reduction_rblock then divides EVERY reduction's R_BLOCK by that cross-loop product, even though each loop's program only holds its OWN M_BLOCK rows. Result: 8x-64x under-sizes of ordinary contiguous, backed, RESIDENT per-program reductions. The mechanical checker reads GREEN every time (no floor-to-1; axes stay tunable >1) -- exactly the under-size blind spot the brief warned about; ALL four were caught only by A/B de-fuse. This is the same conflation family as round-4 finding-2 (cross-loop residency leak into the apply-loop denominator), but on the REDUCTION R_BLOCK sizing path, which was not patched.

TRIGGER boundary precisely characterized: the hole fires iff a fused user-tiled fact has >=2 grid loops where at least one m-axis WIDENS above 1 (a collapse CTA occupancy-widen to 64, or an unpinned hl.tile(m) reduction widening to 16). When ALL grid axes are pinned block_size=1 (K1, K6, K8), m_block_product stays 1 and the seed is byte-identical to standalone (GREEN) -- which is why the existing corpus + round-4 probes never exposed it (every prior multi-loop probe pinned its independent loop to block_size=1: see grid_collapse_fused_indep_loop.py's collapse_plus_indep_usertiled which pins tile_p block_size=1, masking the contamination on the now-2048 primary).

The STANDARD track is GREEN under the same shape (K5): rolled reductions become SEPARATE facts (nRF=2) and reduction_loops is built by-slot per fact, so no cross-loop conflation -- the asymmetry confirms the defect is specific to the user-tiled single-fact fold. Out-of-scope predicates ruled out for every hole: reduced axes are contiguous inner dims (not STRIDED-DIM0), statically backed (not JAGGED), and RESIDENT not grid (not PARTIAL_GRID). Round-4 regression probes re-verified 0/2 RED at HEAD ea24dd1a; the finding-2 apply-loop floor fix still holds in the triple-fusion K9 (normalize axis got 2048, not floored to 1).

holes.explanation: ROOT CAUSE: _m_block_product (triton.py:872) returns the PRODUCT of _m_axis_block_size over ALL fact.m_block_ids, which on a multi-fact kernel spans the grid axes of UNRELATED fused loops. That global m_block is then passed to _reduction_rblock for the primary AND every secondary reducing axis (get_seed_config lines ~1481/1554), where it divides the per-program residency budget (budget = ROW_PERSIST_MAX_BYTES // (m * itemsize * ff), triton.py:1182). A reduction loop that tiles its own M axis at block_size=1 (1 row resident per program) thus gets its r_block shrunk by the FOREIGN loop's M-block: m_block=16 -> r_block clamps 8192->2048 (proven directly: _reduction_rblock(m=16)->2048 vs _reduction_rblock(m=1)->8192). The under-size compounds multiplicatively with each additional fused grid loop (2 loops: 16x->4x rblock cut; 3 loops: 256x->64x). The round-4 Fix 1 scoped the m-collapse override and grid-occupancy to the primary's own loop, and Fix 2 scoped the co-residency PINNED product, but the shared m_block feeding _reduction_rblock is still the global product across all loops -- the same cross-loop-contamination class, one level deeper. NOT a closed predicate: extents are static (not jagged), the reductions are contiguous inner per-row reductions (not strided-dim0), and they are RESIDENT reductions parallelized per-row over a block_size=1 grid (not a tunable PARTIAL_GRID axis). The checker reads GREEN (2048/128 != floor-to-1); only A/B de-fuse exposes it. The existing permanent probe gateT/grid_collapse_fused_indep_loop.py accepts 2048 because its guard threshold is primary_block>64, not the standalone 8192. FIX DIRECTION: size each reduction fact's r_block against the m_block of ITS OWN loop (the m_block_ids that co-occur with that fact's reducing axes), not the global product over every fused loop's grid axis.

sweeps.narrative:
Independent Gate-T adversary, ADVERSARIAL strategy (attack the two round-4 fixes directly). Verified worktree heuristic at ea24dd1a (helion.__file__ under helion-unify). Read both fix diffs (1650a3c6 m-collapse-override primary-unbacked scoping; 9f094896 _pinned_inner_resident_elems reduction-axis exclusion) and the sizing path (_m_block_product, _reduction_rblock, _build_block_sizes, _m_collapse_grid_block). Minted 19 kernels in fresh processes (EFFORT=none, fresh HELION_CACHE_DIR), ran the mechanical checker + A/B de-fuse on each.

FIX 1c (single-loop collapse, bias_grad): confirmed NOT broken -- grid stays occupancy-sized (128<=256 cap), primary inner re-tile sized to the CTA wave, is_m_collapse stays True because the primary IS the unbacked re-tile.

FIX 1a (unbacked-primary-deserves-wide): collapse_few_grid_rows matched its standalone byte-for-byte; no divergence -- the pure-collapse body_live<=1 path sizes r_block to the (capped) CTA wave, which is what a standalone collapse does too.

FIX 1b (backed/unbacked extent-tie routing): this is where the hole surfaced. The fix correctly keeps the collapse grid at 64 and routes the backed loop-2 reduction off the m-collapse override -- BUT the de-fuse A/B showed the loop-2 reduction sized 2048 vs standalone 8192. Drilling in (direct _reduction_rblock calls) traced it to _m_block_product multiplying the FOREIGN collapse loop's m_block (16) into loop-2's residency m_block. I then ISOLATED it with two_indep (two independent per-row reductions, NO collapse at all) -- same 2048 vs 8192 -- proving it is a general multi-fact m_block-contamination bug, not collapse-specific. three_indep shows it compounds to a 64x under-size (8192->128) with 3 fused loops. The EXACT documented finding-1 template (collapse_plus_indep_usertiled) reproduces 2048 vs standalone 8192, and the shipped permanent probe reports green on it (guard threshold 64, not the standalone width) -- so the r4 fix under-corrected by 4x.

FIX 2 (reduction-axis exclusion from co-residency denominator): attacked over-exclusion two ways (grouped_reduce_apply with a wide co-resident reduction; reduce_then_normalize). Both apply/normalize loops sized full-width 8192 identically with and without the co-resident reduction -- no wrongful widening. Architecturally over-exclusion is unreachable: a reduction's RESULT is captured by the primary residency (r_block_resident), not the pinned-feature product, so the only thing the product can still count is a full-extent NON-reduction feature axis (group_size), which I confirmed is still counted in rms_per_block. Fix 2 is sound.

NET: Fix 2 dry; Fix 1 closed the catastrophic 64-floor but left a structural 4x-to-64x reduction under-size from the global _m_block_product, exposed only by A/B de-fuse (checker-green).

holes.explanation: Cross-loop m_block BLEED in _m_block_product (helion/_compiler/autotuner_heuristics/triton.py:872). When a two-level grid-COLLAPSE loop (loop 1, grid axis bid 0 = register_block_size CTA defaulting to 16) is FUSED in one kernel with an INDEPENDENT grid loop (loop 2, grid axis bid 3, block_size=1) whose backed inner reduction the dominant-fact picker selects as primary (bid 4), fact.m_block_ids aggregates BOTH grid axes -> (0,3). _m_block_product multiplies them: bid0=16 * bid3=1 = 16. But the primary reduction lives ONLY in loop 2, whose true co-resident M_BLOCK is 1 (the loops are SEQUENTIAL grid loops, grid_block_ids=[[0],[3]], NOT co-resident). _reduction_rblock then sizes the streamed R_BLOCK with budget = ROW_PERSIST_MAX_BYTES // (m_block * itemsize * ff) = 245760//(16*4*1)=3840 -> prev_pow2 -> 2048, vs the correct 245760//(1*4)=61440 -> clamp to extent (8192 or 4096). So the foreign collapse CTA inflates the residency denominator 16x, under-sizing the independent reduction's R_BLOCK by the foreign m_block factor (2-4x here). This is the SAME cross-loop-bleed CLASS as round-4 findings 1 (grid-occupancy override) and 2 (_pinned_inner_resident_elems co-residency denominator), but on a THIRD unguarded field: the _m_block_product denominator feeding _reduction_rblock. The round-4 finding-1 FIX only gated the floor-to-occupancy-block (is_m_collapse on primary_unbacked) so primary_block no longer floors to 64 -- but it did NOT restore the correct R_BLOCK width, because _m_block_product still sums foreign m-axes. PROOF the round-4 guard misses it: gateT/grid_collapse_fused_indep_loop.py [F1] (the IDENTICAL kernel: x=8192x1024, z=4096x8192) reports primary_block=2048 as GREEN -- its only test is primary_block<=64; 2048>64 passes, yet the standalone de-fuse gives 8192. The mechanical checker reads GREEN (under-size, not FLOOR1_TILED). Found ONLY by A/B de-fuse. Fix direction: _m_block_product (or _reduction_rblock's m_block arg) should multiply only the m_block_ids CO-RESIDENT with the primary reduction's loop (e.g. exclude grid_collapse_block_ids / foreign-loop grid axes), mirroring the round-4 rolled/reduction-role exclusions on the other two denominators. SCOPE confirmation: in-scope (not JAGGED -- Q has static extent; not STRIDED-DIM0 -- z[tile_p,tile_q] is a contiguous inner axis; not PARTIAL_GRID -- the reduction is a resident inner reduction, not over a grid axis).

adjudication.summary: NOT-DRY. All three strategy-divergent sweeps converged on ONE genuine totality hole class: _m_block_product (triton.py:872) cross-loop m-axis bleed. When >=2 reduction loops fuse into a single user-tiled ReductionFact (via register_unrolled_reductions), the fact's m_block_ids aggregates grid axes from DISJOINT loops; _m_block_product cross-multiplies them and feeds the product as m_block to _reduction_rblock, dividing each reduction's R_BLOCK residency budget by foreign loops' M-blocks. Result: 2x-64x under-sizes of ordinary contiguous, backed, RESIDENT per-program reductions, invisible to the mechanical checker (no floor-to-1; axes stay tunable >1) and exposed ONLY by A/B de-fuse. I independently reproduced it three ways: (1) K10 pure two-unpinned-tile reductions, no collapse -> primary 128 vs 8192 (64x), secondary 128 vs 4096 (32x); (2) K3 grid-collapse + independent loop -> 2048 vs 16384 (8x), with an instrumented direct call confirming m_block_product=16 (fused) vs 1 (standalone); (3) sweep-3 dt_collision -> 2048 vs 8192/4096, extent-independent foreign-factor. Source trace confirms the arithmetic exactly (budget=245760/(256*4)=240->128). The round-4 Fix-1 closed the catastrophic floor-to-64 but UNDER-CORRECTED: the shipped regression probe grid_collapse_fused_indep_loop.py accepts 2048 as green because its guard is primary_block<=64 while the standalone is 16384. Standard track (K5) is GREEN under the same shape (separate facts, by-slot reduction_loops), confirming the defect is specific to the user-tiled single-fact fold; Fix-2 (co-residency reduction-axis exclusion) verified sound; JAGGED correctly declines. DIVERGENCE OK: novelty (pure multi-loop fold, no collapse), adversarial (isolated _m_block_product via two_indep/three_indep), and boundary/dtype (bf16/fp16/extreme/jagged) explored genuinely different regions and corroborated rather than duplicated. COVERAGE OK: both round-4 fix regions (multi-loop fusion, extent collision) and both specific fixes were directly attacked. Fix direction: size each reduction fact's r_block against only the m_block_ids co-resident with its own loop, excluding foreign-loop / grid_collapse grid axes -- the same exclusion pattern the round-4 fixes applied to the other two denominators.
